pos.personaBrief: Ajax and Netherlands kept the ball with short passes and made the pitch big (Guide to Football possession-based attack; TFT space), so they seek control of the ball rather than waiting for counters.

pro.personaBrief: Short passing to draw opponents out of position, goalkeeper used as libero, and keeping the ball after winning it point to patient build-up rather than long balls or three-touch finishes.

est.personaBrief: Positional interchange within a kept structure, with space stretched wide and a roaming centre forward (Guide to Football, Spielverlagerung, TFT oscillation), is relational fluidity rather than fixed zones, though not a tight rondo style.

lar.personaBrief: Sources say play was spread to the wings to enlarge the pitch (TFT), with players drifting wide, so width is valued while crossing duels are not the defining route.

blo.personaBrief: Michels wanted hard pressing with an offside trap, a high defensive line and immediate space reduction after losing the ball (Neeskens, TFT, Guide to Football).

mar.personaBrief: The space-based paradigm and compactness suggest zonal thinking, but marking is not verified for Ajax, so I lean zone moderately.

pla.personaBrief: The team played its own proactive, interchange-based model regardless of opponent, and Michels moulded players to it, though he learned balance lessons after the 1969 Milan defeat.

res.personaBrief: Total football prized attacking, proactive play and legacy (1974 lost final remembered), though Michels called football war and wanted trophies; it plays to win away and does not park the bus.

sis.personaBrief: Collective system with everyone defending and attacking, yet Cruyff conducted on the pitch; the star works within the structure and must press.

jog.personaBrief: Players had to be unbelievably fit and adaptable (SI, TFT) as well as technically skilled, so intensity is a basic requirement but technique and intelligence lead.

bas.personaBrief: Ajax's youth system produced the technically gifted group around Cruyff (Guide to Football), so academy players and development were central.

lid.personaBrief: Michels was very strict, with military-style camps and a discipline-first message (TFT, NOS), leaving little room for players to co-decide.
